questions.q: What does version = "~> 5.0" allow Terraform to do?
options: Use only exactly version 5.0 and nothing else
Use any version 5.0 or higher, including 6.x and beyond
Use any version in the 5.x line (5.1, 5.9, etc.), but not jump to 6.0
Use any version lower than 5.0
questions.explain: The ~> pessimistic constraint lets the rightmost version segment increase while blocking the segment to its left, so ~> 5.0 stays within 5.x.

questions.q: Why does a major version bump in a registry module (e.g. 5.x to 6.0) matter?
options: It never matters since all versions behave identically
Semantic versioning treats a major bump as the project's own signal that it may contain breaking changes
It only affects the module's README, not its behavior
Major versions are not allowed on the Terraform Registry
questions.explain: Published modules are expected to follow semantic versioning, where a major version increase signals potential breaking changes.

questions.q: Does a local module, called with source = "./modules/storage-account", take a version argument?
options: Yes, it is required for all modules regardless of source
No — there is no published release to pin since the module's code lives in the same repository
Only if the module has outputs
Only on Windows systems
questions.explain: version applies to modules with published, versioned releases (like registry sources). A local path has no separate release to pin.

questions.q: What is the standard file layout convention for a reusable Terraform module?
options: A single config.tf file containing everything
main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and README.md
index.tf, app.tf, and settings.json
There is no convention; Terraform enforces a fixed structure
questions.explain: The community convention separates resources (main.tf), inputs (variables.tf), outputs (outputs.tf), and documentation (README.md).

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when should a resource be extracted into its own module rather than left inline?
options: Always, for consistency across every configuration
Never — modules should only be used for registry sources
When the same combination of resources needs to exist more than once, or the configuration is complex enough that hiding it behind variables simplifies the root module
Only when the resource belongs to a free-tier service
questions.explain: Modules pay off when a pattern repeats (e.g. across dev/staging/prod) or when complexity justifies hiding internals behind an interface; over-modularizing adds indirection without benefit.
